questions.q: The minimum value of $\alpha$ for which the equation $\dfrac{4}{sinx} + \dfrac{1}{1 - sinx} = \alpha$ has at least one solution in $\left(0, \dfrac{\pi}{2}\right)$ is______.
questions.solution:
Let

$f\left(x\right) = \dfrac{4}{sinx} + \dfrac{1}{1 - sinx}$

$⇒ f\left(x\right) = \dfrac{4}{sinx} + \dfrac{1 + sinx}{1 - \sin^{2}x}$

$⇒ f\left(x\right) = 4cosecx + {sec}^{2}x + tanxsecx$

$⇒ {f}^{'}\left(x\right) = \dfrac{- 4cosx}{\sin^{2}x} + \dfrac{2sinx + 1}{\cos^{3}x} + \dfrac{\sin^{2}x}{\cos^{3}x}$

$⇒ {f}^{'}\left(x\right) = \dfrac{- 4cosx}{\sin^{2}x} + \dfrac{{\left(sinx + 1\right)}^{2}}{\cos^{3}x}$

$⇒ {f}^{' '}\left(x\right) = - 4\left[\dfrac{- \sin^{3}x - 2sinx\cos^{2}x}{\sin^{4}x}\right] + \dfrac{2\left(sinx + 1\right)\cos^{4}x + 3\cos^{2}xsinx{\left(sinx + 1\right)}^{2}}{\cos^{6}x}$

$⇒ {f}^{' '}\left(x\right) = - 4\left[\dfrac{- \sin^{3}x - 2sinx\left(1 - \sin^{2}x\right)}{\sin^{4}x}\right] + \dfrac{2\left(sinx + 1\right){\left(1 - \sin^{2}x\right)}^{2} + 3\left(1 - \sin^{2}x\right)sinx{\left(sinx + 1\right)}^{2}}{{\left(1 - \sin^{2}x\right)}^{3}}$

For critical points,

${f}^{'}\left(x\right) = 0$

$⇒ \dfrac{{\left(sinx + 1\right)}^{2}}{\cos^{3}x} = \dfrac{4cosx}{\sin^{2}x}$

$⇒ \sin^{2}x{\left(sinx + 1\right)}^{2} = 4\cos^{4}x$

$⇒ sinx\left(sinx + 1\right) = 2\cos^{2}x$

$⇒ \sin^{2}x + sinx = 2 - 2\sin^{2}x$

$⇒ 3\sin^{2}x + sinx - 2 = 0$

$⇒ 3\sin^{2}x + 3sinx - 2sinx - 2 = 0$

$⇒ \left(3sinx - 2\right)\left(sinx + 1\right) = 0$

$⇒ sinx = \dfrac{2}{3}$

Since, $sinx > 0 ∀ x \in \left(0, \dfrac{\pi}{2}\right)$

Now, at $sinx = \dfrac{2}{3}$, we get

$⇒ {f}^{' '}\left(x\right) = - 4\left[\dfrac{- \dfrac{8}{27} - \dfrac{4}{3}\left(1 - \dfrac{4}{9}\right)}{\dfrac{16}{81}}\right] + \dfrac{2 \times \dfrac{5}{3}{\left(1 - \dfrac{4}{9}\right)}^{2} + 3\left(1 - \dfrac{4}{9}\right) \times \dfrac{2}{3} \times \dfrac{25}{9}}{{\left(1 - \dfrac{4}{9}\right)}^{3}}$

$⇒ {f}^{' '}\left(x\right) = \left[4\left[\dfrac{28}{27} \times \dfrac{81}{16}\right] + \dfrac{2 \times \dfrac{5}{3}{\left(\dfrac{5}{9}\right)}^{2} + 3\left(\dfrac{5}{9}\right) \times \dfrac{2}{3} \times \dfrac{25}{9}}{{\left(\dfrac{5}{9}\right)}^{3}}\right] > 0$

Hence, it is the point of minima.

$∴ f{\left(x\right)}_{min} = \dfrac{4}{\dfrac{2}{3}} + \dfrac{1}{1 - \dfrac{2}{3}} = 9$

$f{\left(x\right)}_{max} \to \infty$

$f\left(x\right)$ is continuous function

$∴ {\alpha}_{min} = 9$

questions.solution:
Given,

${x}^{5}\left({x}^{3} - {x}^{2} - x + 1\right) + x\left(3{x}^{3} - 4{x}^{2} - 2x + 4\right) - 1 = 0$

Now on rearranging we get

$⇒ {x}^{8} - {x}^{7} - {x}^{6} + {x}^{5} + 3{x}^{4} - 4{x}^{3} - 2{x}^{2} + 4x - 1 = 0$

$⇒ {x}^{7}\left(x - 1\right) - {x}^{5}\left(x - 1\right) + 3{x}^{3}\left(x - 1\right) - x\left({x}^{2} - 1\right) - 2x\left(x - 1\right) + x - 1 = 0$

$⇒ \left(x - 1\right)\left({x}^{7} - {x}^{5} + 3{x}^{3} - x\left(x + 1\right) - 2x + 1\right) = 0$

$⇒ \left(x - 1\right)\left({x}^{5}\left({x}^{2} - 1\right) + 3x\left({x}^{2} - 1\right) - 1\left({x}^{2} - 1\right)\right) = 0$

$⇒ \left({x}^{2} - 1\right)\left(x - 1\right)\left({x}^{5} + 3x - 1\right) = 0$

From above equation it is clearly visible that the root are $x = \pm 1$ and for ${x}^{5} + 3x - 1$

Let $f\left(x\right) = {x}^{5} + 3x - 1$, ${f}^{'}\left(x\right) = 5{x}^{4} + 3$

${f}^{'}\left(x\right) > 0 ∀ x \in R$, hence it is monotonic in nature so it will have only one root other than $1 \text{ and } - 1$.

Hence $3$ real distinct roots.

questions.q: Let $f\left(x\right) = \left|\left(x - 1\right)\left({x}^{2} - 2x - 3\right)\right| + x - 3, x \in \mathbb{R}$. If $m$ and $M$ are respectively the number of points of local minimum and local maximum of $f$ in the interval $\left(0, 4\right)$, then $m + M$ is equal to _____.
questions.solution:
Given,

$f\left(x\right) = \left|\left(x - 1\right)\left(x + 1\right)\left(x - 3\right)\right| + \left(x - 3\right)$

$f\left(x\right) = \left\{\begin{cases}\left(x - 3\right)\left({x}^{2}\right), & 3 \le x \le 4 \\ \left(x - 3\right)\left(2 - {x}^{2}\right), & 1 \le x < 3 \\ \left(x - 3\right)\left({x}^{2}\right), & 0 < x < 1\end{cases}\right$

${f}^{'}\left(x\right) = \left\{\begin{cases}3{x}^{2} - 6x, & 3 < x < 4 \\ - 3{x}^{2} + 6x + 2, & 1 < x < 3 \\ 3{x}^{2} - 6x, & 0 < x < 1\end{cases}\right$

${f}^{'}\left({3}^{+}\right) > 0{f}^{'}\left({3}^{-}\right) < 0 \to$ Minimum

${f}^{'}\left({1}^{+}\right) > 0{f}^{'}\left({1}^{-}\right) < 0 \to$ Minimum

For $x \in \left(1, 3\right), {f}^{'}\left(x\right) = 0$ at one point $\to$ Maximum

For $x \in \left(3, 4\right), {f}^{'}\left(x\right) \ne 0$

For $x \in \left(0, 1\right), {f}^{'}\left(x\right) + 0$

So points of minima are $2$, so $m = 2$

and point of maxima is $1$, so $M = 1$

So, $M + n = 3$

questions.q: Let the function $f\left(x\right) = 2{x}^{2} - {\log}_{e}x, x > 0$, be decreasing in $\left(0, a\right)$ and increasing in $\left(a, 4\right)$. A tangent to the parabola ${y}^{2} = 4ax$ at a point $P$ on it passes through the point $\left(8a, 8a - 1\right)$ but does not pass through the point $\left(- \dfrac{1}{a}, 0\right)$. If the equation of the normal at $P$ is $\dfrac{x}{\alpha} + \dfrac{y}{\beta} = 1$, then $\alpha + \beta$ is equal to
questions.solution:
Given, $f\left(x\right) = 2{x}^{2} - {\log}_{e}x$

$⇒ {f}^{'}\left(x\right) = 4x - \dfrac{1}{x}$

$⇒ {f}^{'}\left(x\right) = \dfrac{4{x}^{2} - 1}{x}$

$⇒ {f}^{'}\left(x\right) = 0 ⇒ 4{x}^{2} - 1 = 0 ⇒ x = \pm \dfrac{1}{2}$

But given $x > 0\text{so}x = \dfrac{1}{2}$

So function is decreasing in $\left(0, \dfrac{1}{2}\right)$ and increasing in the interval $\left(\dfrac{1}{2}, \infty\right)$

So, $a = \dfrac{1}{2}$

Now equation of parabola will be ${y}^{2} = 2x$

Now tangent to ${y}^{2} = 2x$ will be given by,

$y = mx + \dfrac{1}{2m}$, given this tangent passes through $\left(8a, 8a - 1\right) ≡ \left(4, 3\right)$,

So $3 = 4m + \dfrac{1}{2m}$

$⇒ m = \dfrac{1}{2}\text{or}\dfrac{1}{4}$

So equation of tangent are $y = \dfrac{x}{2} + 1\text{or}y = \dfrac{x}{4} + 2$

But $y = \dfrac{x}{2} + 1$ passes through $\left(- 2, 0\right)$ so rejected as given in the question.

Now equation of normal at $P$ will be,

$y = - 4x - 2\left(\dfrac{1}{2}\right)\left(- 4\right) - \dfrac{1}{2}{\left(- 4\right)}^{3}$ $\left\{\text{as slope of normal =}\dfrac{- 1}{\dfrac{1}{4}}\text{=-4}\right\}$

$⇒ y = - 4x + 4 + 32$

$⇒ y + 4x = 36$

$⇒ \dfrac{x}{9} + \dfrac{y}{36} = 1$

So, $\alpha = 9, \beta = 36$

So, $\alpha + \beta = 45$

We have $x + 6 = {x}^{2}$

$⇒ {x}^{2} - x - 6 = 0$

$⇒ \left(x - 3\right)\left(x + 2\right) = 0$

$⇒ x = 3 \text{ and } - 2 .$

Also, $\sqrt{x} = {x}^{2}$

$⇒ {x}^{2} - \sqrt{x} = 0$

$⇒ \sqrt{x}\left(x\dfrac{3}{2} - 1\right) = 0$

$⇒ x = 0 \text{ and } x = 1 .$

Hence, the region bounded by $f\left(x\right)$ is given by the following graph.

Hence, the area bounded by $y = f ( x )$ and $x$-axis is

$A = {∫}_{- 3}^{- 2} ( x + 6 ) dx + {∫}_{- 2}^{0}{x}^{2}dx + {∫}_{0}^{1}\sqrt{x}dx$

$⇒ A = {\left(\dfrac{{x}^{2}}{2} + 6x\right)}_{- 3}^{- 2} + {\left(\dfrac{{x}^{3}}{3}\right)}_{- 2}^{0} + {\left(\dfrac{2{x}^{\dfrac{3}{2}}}{3}\right)}_{0}^{1}$

$⇒ A = \left(\dfrac{4}{2} - 12 - \left(\dfrac{9}{2} - 18\right)\right) + \left(\dfrac{0 + 8}{3}\right) + \left(\dfrac{2 \times 1 - 0}{3}\right)$

$⇒ A = - 10 + \dfrac{27}{2} + \dfrac{8}{3} + \dfrac{2}{3}$

$⇒ A = \dfrac{41}{6}$ sq units.

$⇒ 6A = 41 .$

Let $f: R \to R$ be a function defined as $f\left(x\right) = \left\{\begin{cases}3\left(1 - \dfrac{| x |}{2}\right) & \text{if} & | x | \le 2 \\ 0 & \text{if} & | x | > 2\end{cases}\right .$

Let $g: R \to R$ be given by $g ( x ) = f ( x + 2 ) - f ( x - 2 ) .$ If $n$ and $m$ denote the number of points in $R$ where $g$ is not continuous and not differentiable, respectively, then $n + m$ is equal to ________.
questions.solution:
The given function is $f\left(x\right) = \left\{\begin{cases}3\left(1 - \dfrac{| x |}{2}\right) & if & | x | \le 2 \\ 0 & if & | x | > 2\end{cases}\right$

By using the definition of modulus function, we have $\left|x\right| = \left\{\begin{cases}x, & x \ge 0 \\ - x, & x < 0\end{cases}\right$ and also, we know that if $\left|x\right| \le a, ⇒ - a \le x \le a$ and if $\left|x\right| > a, ⇒ x a,$

$⇒ f\left(x\right) = \left\{\begin{cases}3\left(1 + \dfrac{x}{2}\right), & - 2 \le x \le 0 \\ 3\left(1 - \dfrac{x}{2}\right), & 0 xorx > 2\end{cases}\right$

Now, $f\left(x - 2\right) = \left\{\begin{cases}3\left(1 + \dfrac{x - 2}{2}\right), & - 2 \le x - 2 \le 0 \\ 3\left(1 - \dfrac{x - 2}{2}\right), & 0 x - 2orx - 2 > 2\end{cases}\right$

$⇒ f\left(x - 2\right) = \left\{\begin{cases}\dfrac{3x}{2}, & 0 \le x \le 2 \\ 6 - \dfrac{3x}{2}, & 2 xorx > 4\end{cases}\right$

And, $f\left(x + 2\right) = \left\{\begin{cases}3\left(1 + \dfrac{x + 2}{2}\right), & - 2 \le x + 2 \le 0 \\ 3\left(1 - \dfrac{x + 2}{2}\right), & 0 x + 2orx + 2 > 2\end{cases}\right$

$⇒ f\left(x + 2\right) = \left\{\begin{cases}6 + \dfrac{3x}{2}, & - 4 \le x \le - 2 \\ - \dfrac{3x}{2}, & - 2 xorx > 0\end{cases}\right$

Hence, $g\left(x\right) = f\left(x + 2\right) - f\left(x - 2\right) = \left\{\begin{array}{ll}\dfrac{3x}{2} + 6, - 4 \le x \le - 2 \\ - \dfrac{3x}{2}, - 2 < x < 2 \\ \dfrac{3x}{2} - 6, 2 \le x \le 4 \\ 0, x \in ( - \infty , - 4 ) ∪ ( 4, \infty )\end{array}\right$

The graph of $g\left(x\right)$ is given below

From the graph we can observe that the function $g\left(x\right)$ is continuous everywhere, hence the number of points where $g\left(x\right)$ is not continuos is $n = 0$ and the graph has sharp corners at the points $\left(- 4, 0\right), \left(4, 0\right), \left(- 2, 3\right) \text{ and } \left(2, - 3\right)$ thus the number of points where $g\left(x\right)$ is not differentiable are $m = 4$

$⇒ n + m = 4 .$

questions.q: Suppose f is a function satisfying $f ( x + y ) = f ( x ) + f ( y )$ for  all $x, y \in \mathbb{N}$ and $f ( 1 ) = \dfrac{1}{5}$. If $\mathop{∑}_{n = 1}^{m}\dfrac{f ( n )}{n ( n + 1 ) ( n + 2 )} = \dfrac{1}{12}$ then $m$ is equal to ______.
questions.solution:
Given,

$f\left(x + y\right) = f\left(x\right) + f\left(y\right) \text{ and } f\left(1\right) = \dfrac{1}{5}$

Now solving the given functional equation by taking $x = 1 \text{ and } y = 1$ we get,

$f\left(1 + 1\right) = f\left(1\right) + f\left(1\right)$

$⇒ f\left(2\right) = \dfrac{2}{5}\left\{\text{as}f\left(1\right) = \dfrac{1}{5}\right\}$

Now taking $x = 2 \text{ and } y = 1$ we get,

$f\left(3\right) = \dfrac{2}{5} + \dfrac{1}{5} ⇒ f\left(3\right) = \dfrac{3}{5}$

Hence, $f\left(x\right) = \dfrac{x}{5}$

Now solving $\mathop{∑}_{n = 1}^{m}\dfrac{f\left(n\right)}{n\left(n + 1\right)\left(n + 2\right)} = \dfrac{1}{12}$

$⇒ \mathop{∑}_{n = 1}^{m}\dfrac{\dfrac{n}{5}}{n\left(n + 1\right)\left(n + 2\right)} = \dfrac{1}{12}$

$⇒ \dfrac{1}{5}\mathop{∑}_{n = 1}^{m}\dfrac{1}{\left(n + 1\right)\left(n + 2\right)} = \dfrac{1}{12}$

$⇒ \dfrac{1}{5}\mathop{∑}_{n = 1}^{m}\dfrac{1}{\left(n + 1\right)} - \dfrac{1}{\left(n + 2\right)} = \dfrac{1}{12}$

$⇒ \dfrac{1}{5}\left[\dfrac{1}{2} - \dfrac{1}{m + 2}\right] = \dfrac{1}{12}$

$⇒ \left[\dfrac{m}{2\left(m + 2\right)}\right] = \dfrac{5}{12}$

$⇒ 12m = 10\left(m + 2\right)$

$⇒ m = 10$

questions.q: Let $y = y\left(x\right)$ be the solution of the differential equation $\dfrac{dy}{dx} = \dfrac{4{y}^{3} + 2y{x}^{2}}{3x{y}^{2} + {x}^{3}}, y\left(1\right) = 1$. If for some $n \in N, y\left(2\right) \in [ n - 1, n )$, then $n$ is equal to _______.
questions.solution:
Given,

$\dfrac{dy}{dx} = \dfrac{y}{x}\dfrac{\left(4{y}^{2} + 2{x}^{2}\right)}{\left(3{y}^{2} + {x}^{2}\right)}$

Let $y = vx$

$⇒ \dfrac{dy}{dx} = v + x\dfrac{dv}{dx}$

So, $\dfrac{dy}{dx} = \dfrac{y}{x}\dfrac{\left(4{y}^{2} + 2{x}^{2}\right)}{\left(3{y}^{2} + {x}^{2}\right)}$

$⇒ v + x\dfrac{dv}{dx} = \dfrac{v\left(4{v}^{2} + 2\right)}{\left(3{v}^{2} + 1\right)}$

$⇒ x\dfrac{dv}{dx} = v\left(\dfrac{\left(4{v}^{2} + 2 - 3{v}^{2} - 1\right)}{3{v}^{2} + 1}\right)$

$⇒ ∫ \left(3{v}^{2} + 1\right)\dfrac{dv}{{v}^{3} + v} = ∫ \dfrac{dx}{x}$

$⇒ ln\left|{v}^{3} + v\right| = lnx + c$

$⇒ ln\left|{\left(\dfrac{y}{x}\right)}^{3} + \left(\dfrac{y}{x}\right)\right| = lnx + c$

Given, $y\left(1\right) = 1$

$⇒ c = ln2$

So the equation becomes $ln\left|{\left(\dfrac{y}{x}\right)}^{3} + \left(\dfrac{y}{x}\right)\right| = lnx + ln2$

Now for $y\left(2\right)$

So putting $x = 2$ in $ln\left|{\left(\dfrac{y}{x}\right)}^{3} + \left(\dfrac{y}{x}\right)\right| = lnx + ln2$

We get, $ln\left(\dfrac{{y}^{3}}{8} + \dfrac{y}{2}\right) = 2ln2 ⇒ \dfrac{{y}^{3}}{8} + \dfrac{y}{2} = 4$

$⇒ \left[y\left(2\right)\right] = 2$

So, $y\left(2\right) \in [ 2, 3 )$

So on comparing with $y\left(2\right) \in [ n - 1, n )$

$⇒ n = 3$

Now rewriting equation (i) again we get,

Now $\dfrac{{d}^{2}x}{d{y}^{2}} = \dfrac{d}{dx}\left({\left({x}^{{x}^{2} + 1}\left(1 + 2lnx\right)\right)}^{- 1}\right)\dfrac{dx}{dy}$

Given,

$\dfrac{dy}{dx} - y = 2 - {e}^{- x}$

Linear differential equation,

So, $I . F . = {e}^{- ∫ dx} = {e}^{- x}$

Now solution of differential equation is given by

$y \times IF = ∫ \left(2 - {e}^{- x}\right) \times IFdx$

$⇒ y{e}^{- x} = ∫ \left(2 - {e}^{- x}\right){e}^{- x}dx$

$⇒ y{e}^{- x} = ∫ \left(2{e}^{- x} - {e}^{- 2x}\right)dx$

$⇒ y{e}^{- x} = - 2{e}^{- x} + \dfrac{{e}^{- 2x}}{2} + C$

$⇒ y = - 2 + \dfrac{{e}^{- x}}{2} + C{e}^{x}$

Given $\lim_{x \to \infty}y$ is finite

So, $\lim_{x \to \infty}\left(- 2 + \dfrac{{e}^{- x}}{2} + C \cdot {e}^{x}\right) \to$finite

This is possible only when $C = 0$

Hence$y = y\left(x\right) = - 2 + \dfrac{{e}^{- x}}{2}$

Now finding the slope $\dfrac{dy}{dx} = - \dfrac{1}{2}{e}^{- x}$

${\dfrac{dy}{dx}}_{x = 0} = - \dfrac{1}{2} = m, y\left(0\right) = - 2 + \dfrac{1}{2} = \dfrac{- 3}{2}$

Now equation of tangent will be,

$y + \dfrac{3}{2} = - \dfrac{1}{2}\left(x - 0\right)$

$⇒ x + 2y = - 3$

x-intercept $a = - 3,$ y-intercept $b = \dfrac{- 3}{2}$

So, $a - 4b = - 3 + 6 = 3$

questions.solution:
Given,

$f\left(mn\right) = f\left(m\right) \cdot f\left(n\right)$

Put $m = 1,$ then $f\left(1 \cdot n\right) = f\left(1\right) \cdot f\left(n\right) ⇒ f\left(1\right) = 1\left\{f\left(n\right) \ne 0\right\}$

Put $m = n = 2$

$f\left(4\right) = f\left(2\right) \cdot f\left(2\right)$

If $f\left(2\right) = 1,$ then $f\left(4\right) = 1$ and if $f\left(2\right) = 2,$ then $f\left(4\right) = 4$

Put $m = 2, n = 3$

$f\left(6\right) = f\left(2\right) \cdot f\left(3\right)$

If $f\left(2\right) = 1,$ then $f\left(3\right)$ can be any value between $1$ to $7$

If $f\left(2\right) = 2,$ then $f\left(3\right)$ can be $1$ or $2$ or $3$

Similarly $f\left(5\right), f\left(7\right)$ can take any value from $\left\{1, 2, . . . , 7\right\}$

So, total number of function $= \left(1 \times 1 \times 7 \times 1 \times 7 \times 1 \times 7\right) + \left(1 \times 1 \times 3 \times 1 \times 7 \times 1 \times 7\right)$

$= 490$

questions.solution:
We have,

$\lim_{x \to 0}\left[\dfrac{\alphax{e}^{x} - \beta{\log}_{e} ( 1 + x ) + \gamma{x}^{2}{e}^{- x}}{x\sin^{2}x}\right] = 10$

$⇒ \lim_{x \to 0}\left[\dfrac{\alphax\left(1 + x + \dfrac{{x}^{2}}{2 !} + . .\right) - \beta\left(x - \dfrac{{x}^{2}}{2} + \dfrac{{x}^{3}}{3} - . . .\right) + \gamma{x}^{2}\left(1 - x + \dfrac{{x}^{2}}{2 !} - . .\right)}{{x}^{3}\left(\dfrac{\sin^{2}x}{{x}^{2}}\right)}\right] = 10$

$⇒ \lim_{x \to 0}\left[\dfrac{\alphax\left(1 + x + \dfrac{{x}^{2}}{2}\right) - \beta\left(x - \dfrac{{x}^{2}}{2} + \dfrac{{x}^{3}}{3}\right) + \gamma{x}^{2}\left(1 - x\right)}{{x}^{3}}\right] = 10$

Neglecting higher powers.

$\lim_{x \to 0}\dfrac{x ( \alpha - \beta ) + {x}^{2}\left(\alpha + \dfrac{\beta}{2} + \gamma\right) + {x}^{3}\left(\dfrac{\alpha}{2} - \dfrac{\beta}{3} - \gamma\right)}{{x}^{3}} = 10$

For limit to exist

$\alpha - \beta = 0$

$\alpha + \dfrac{\beta}{2} + \gamma = 0$

$\dfrac{\alpha}{2} - \dfrac{\beta}{3} - \gamma = 10 \ldots \left(i\right)$

$\beta = \alpha, \gamma = - \dfrac{3\alpha}{2}$

$\dfrac{\alpha}{2} - \dfrac{\alpha}{3} + \dfrac{3\alpha}{2} = 10$

$⇒ \dfrac{\alpha}{6} + \dfrac{3\alpha}{2} = 10$

$⇒ \dfrac{\alpha + 9\alpha}{6} = 10$

$⇒ \alpha = 6$

Hence,

$\alpha = 6, \beta = 6, \gamma = - 9$

$⇒ \alpha + \beta + \gamma = 3$

questions.solution:
We know that,

By demorgan's law ${\left(B ∪ C\right)}^{'} = {B}^{'} ∩ {C}^{'}$

${B}^{'}$ is a set containing sub sets of $A$ containing element $1$ and not containing $2$.

And ${C}^{'}$ is a set containing subsets of $A$ whose sum of elements is not prime.

So, we need to calculate number of subsets of $\left\{3, 4, 5, 6, 7\right\}$ whose sum of elements plus $1$ is composite.

Number of such $5$ elements subset $= 1$

Number of such $4$ elements subset $= 3$ (except selecting $3$ or $7$)

Number of such $3$ elements subset $= 6$ (except selecting $\left\{3, 4, 5\right\}, \left\{3, 6, 7\right\}, \left\{4, 5, 7\right\}$ or $\left\{5, 6, 7\right\}$)

Number of such $2$ elements subset $= 7$ (except selecting $\left\{3, 7\right\}, \left\{4, 6\right\}, \left\{5, 7\right\}$)

Number of such $1$ elements subset $= 3$ (except selecting $\left\{4\right\}$ or $\left\{6\right\}$)

Number of such $0$ elements subset $= 1$

So, number of elements in $n\left({B}^{'} ∩ {C}^{'}\right) = 1 + 3 + 6 + 7 + 3 + 1 = 21$

questions.question: Let $A = \left\{1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7\right\}$. Define $B =${$T ⊆ A$: either $1 \notin T$ or $2 \in T$} and $C =${$T ⊆ A: T$ the sum of all the elements of $T$ is a prime number.} Then the number of elements in the set $B ∪ C$ is _______.
questions.explanation:
We know that,

By demorgan's law ${\left(B ∪ C\right)}^{'} = {B}^{'} ∩ {C}^{'}$

${B}^{'}$ is a set containing sub sets of $A$ containing element $1$ and not containing $2$.

And ${C}^{'}$ is a set containing subsets of $A$ whose sum of elements is not prime.

So, we need to calculate number of subsets of $\left\{3, 4, 5, 6, 7\right\}$ whose sum of elements plus $1$ is composite.

Number of such $5$ elements subset $= 1$

Number of such $4$ elements subset $= 3$ (except selecting $3$ or $7$)

Number of such $3$ elements subset $= 6$ (except selecting $\left\{3, 4, 5\right\}, \left\{3, 6, 7\right\}, \left\{4, 5, 7\right\}$ or $\left\{5, 6, 7\right\}$)

Number of such $2$ elements subset $= 7$ (except selecting $\left\{3, 7\right\}, \left\{4, 6\right\}, \left\{5, 7\right\}$)

Number of such $1$ elements subset $= 3$ (except selecting $\left\{4\right\}$ or $\left\{6\right\}$)

Number of such $0$ elements subset $= 1$

So, number of elements in $n\left({B}^{'} ∩ {C}^{'}\right) = 1 + 3 + 6 + 7 + 3 + 1 = 21$

And number of elements in $n\left(B ∩ C\right) = {2}^{7} - 21 = 107$

questions.q: Let $A = \left\{1, 2, 3, 4\right\}$ and $R$ be a relation on the set $A \times A$ defined by $R = \left\{\left(\left(a, b\right), \left(c, d\right)\right): 2a + 3b = 4c + 5d\right\}$. Then the number of elements in $R$ is _________.
questions.solution:
Given,

Set $A = \left\{1, 2, 3, 4\right\}$

And relation on $A \times A$ as $2a + 3b = 4c + 5d$

Now, Maximum value of $2a + 3b = 20$ at $\left(4, 4\right)$

And Minimum value of $4c + 5d = 9$ at $\left(1, 1\right)$

So, $4c + 5d$ can be equal to $9, 13, 14, 17, 18, 19$

Now $2a + 3b$ can be $9$ if $\left(a, b\right) = \left(3, 1\right) ⇒ \left(c, d\right) = \left(1, 1\right)$

Similarly, $2a + 3b$ can be $13$, if $\left(a, b\right) = \left(2, 3\right) ⇒ \left(c, d\right) = \left(2, 1\right)$

And $2a + 3b$ can be $14$, if $\left(a, b\right) = \left(4, 2\right)\text{or}\left(1, 4\right)$

$⇒ \left(c, d\right) = \left(1, 2\right)$

Similarly, $2a + 3b$ can be $17$, if $\left(a, b\right) = \left(4, 3\right) ⇒$ $\left(c, d\right) = \left(3, 1\right)$

And $2a + 3b$ can be $18$ if $\left(a, b\right) = \left(3, 4\right) ⇒$

$\left(c, d\right) = \left(2, 2\right)$

Hence, there are total $6$ elements which satisfy the given relation.

questions.solution:
Here, $A = \left\{2, 4, 6, . . . . 50\right\}$ and $B = \left\{7, 14, . . . 49\right\}$

Required smallest subset is $A ∪ B$.

So, $n\left(A ∪ B\right) = n\left(A\right) + n\left(B\right) - n\left(A ∩ B\right)$
$= 25 + 7 - 3$
$= 29$.
